what_it_does: GCStack and GCScaler are tools for analyzing GPU performance bottlenecks. Today's GPU analysis tracks what stalls the GPU (waiting for memory, waiting for synchronization, etc.) but uses a simplification: each cycle is attributed to only the single worst bottleneck, missing cases where multiple stalls occur simultaneously. GCStack records every stall that happens in each cycle, creating a fine-grained profile. GCScaler then uses mathematical scaling models to project these profiles onto different GPU designs without re-running expensive simulations: it analytically adjusts timing estimates for memory stalls and synchronization stalls independently. Combined, they enable exploring 1,000 GPU design variants from a single simulation trace—engineers can ask 'what if we doubled memory bandwidth?' or 'what if we increased compute units?' and get accurate predictions instantly.
